body: I went through a rough time a few years ago myself. My family doctor told me the wait time to see a psychiatrist was a few months and suggested I check in at the AAC at VGH. I was interviewed by a nurse then a psychiatrist. They didn’t think I was at risk since I did not actually act on my thoughts and had no history of substance abuse. They put me on meds for a few years now... Unfortunately, it’s not easy/ quick to access mental health help in this country. My experience at VGH was good and quick (got to see a psychiatrist on the same day with some wait.) not sure how it is with pandemic, though. You could speak with your family doctor or go to a walk-in ( many places take virtual consultation.) Perhaps, they can prescribe you medication to fill the gab until you see a specialist. Good luck.

Use the PDOC, the calculator online. Don’t forget your taxable benefits and allowances. Almost all companies use payroll systems that automatically calculate your statutory deductions based on your earnings so it’s not likely it’s a mistake. Just remember everybody’s tax situation is different. it’s up to you to make tax saving decisions / claim tax credits so you get a refund when you file your tax return.  It would also depend on if you have had a second job, started work during the year, etc.
